reference.title: Worker process counts
reference.shortdesc: Use worker count environment variables to set how many parallel processes handle registry, web UI, and security scanning requests in Red Hat Quay.

section.p: If not explicitly set, Red Hat Quay calculates the number of worker processes automatically based on the number of available CPU cores. While this dynamic scaling can optimize performance on larger machines, it might also lead to unnecessary resource usage in smaller environments.
In Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform deployments, the Operator sets the following default values:

entry.p: Generic override for number of processes
Specifies the number of processes to handle Registry requests within the Quay container. Values: Integer between 8 and 64
Specifies the number of processes to handle UI/Web requests within the container. Values: Integer between 2 and 32

Specifies the number of processes to handle Security Scanning (e.g. Clair) integration within the container. Values: Integer. Because the Operator specifies 2 vCPUs for resource requests and limits, setting this value between 2 and 4 is safe. However, users can run more, for example, 16, if warranted.

p.b: Worker count configuration for standalone Red Hat Quay deployments
Worker count configuration for Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform

section.codeblock: env: - name: WORKER_COUNT value: "10" - name: WORKER_COUNT_REGISTRY value: "16" - name: WORKER_COUNT_WEB value: "8" - name: WORKER_COUNT_SECSCAN value: "4"
